Here’s a highly advanced Video Anomaly Detection project using Keras, combining a ConvLSTM-Autoencoder with a Transformer-based self-attention module. It’s very different from previous projects and suitable for a seasoned professional like yourself. 🧠

Project Title: ai-ml-ds-VidAnomTrans‑QWl7
Filename: video_anomaly_detection_transformer.py

Short Description:
Detect anomalies in surveillance-style video streams by reconstructing normal frames using a ConvLSTM autoencoder enhanced with Transformer-based attention. The model learns standard temporal and spatial patterns; deviations in reconstruction signal anomalies.

# video_anomaly_detection_transformer.py

import os
import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers
import cv2

# Types
FrameSeq = np.ndarray  # shape (seq_len, H, W, C)
BatchFrames = tf.Tensor  # shape (batch, seq, H, W, C)

# PARAMETERS
SEQ_LEN: int = 10
IMG_H: int = 128
IMG_W: int = 128
CHANNELS: int = 1
BATCH_SIZE: int = 4
EPOCHS: int = 50
LR: float = 1e-4

# Dummy data loader
def generate_fake_videos(batch_size: int=BATCH_SIZE) -> FrameSeq:
    while True:
        yield np.random.rand(batch_size, SEQ_LEN, IMG_H, IMG_W, CHANNELS).astype('float32')

# Transformer Block
def transformer_encoder(inputs: BatchFrames, head_size: int=64, num_heads: int=4, ff_dim: int=128, dropout: float=0.1):
    x = layers.MultiHeadAttention(num_heads=num_heads, key_dim=head_size)(inputs, inputs)
    x = layers.Dropout(dropout)(x)
    x = layers.LayerNormalization(epsilon=1e-6)(x + inputs)
    ff = layers.Conv1D(filters=ff_dim, kernel_size=1, activation='relu')(x)
    ff = layers.Dropout(dropout)(ff)
    ff = layers.Conv1D(filters=inputs.shape[-1], kernel_size=1)(ff)
    return layers.LayerNormalization(epsilon=1e-6)(x + ff)

# Build model
inp: keras.Input = keras.Input(shape=(SEQ_LEN, IMG_H, IMG_W, CHANNELS), name='video_input')
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.Conv2D(32, 3, padding='same', activation='relu'))(inp)
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.MaxPooling2D())(x)
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.Conv2D(64, 3, padding='same', activation='relu'))(x)
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.MaxPooling2D())(x)
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.Conv2D(128, 3, padding='same', activation='relu'))(x)
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.MaxPooling2D())(x)

# Flatten spatial dims
shape_before: tuple = x.shape.as_list()
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.Flatten())(x)
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.Dense(256, activation='relu'))(x)

# Transformer Encoder stack
for _ in range(2):
    x = transformer_encoder(x, head_size=64, num_heads=4, ff_dim=256, dropout=0.1)

# Decoder reshaping
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.Dense(np.prod(shape_before[2:]), activation='relu'))(x)
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.Reshape(shape_before[2:]))(x)
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.UpSampling2D())(x)
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.Conv2DTranspose(128,3,padding='same', activation='relu'))(x)
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.UpSampling2D())(x)
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.Conv2DTranspose(64,3,padding='same', activation='relu'))(x)
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.UpSampling2D())(x)
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.Conv2DTranspose(32,3,padding='same', activation='relu'))(x)
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.Conv2D(CHANNELS,3,padding='same', activation='sigmoid'))(x)

model: keras.Model = keras.Model(inputs=inp, outputs=x)
model.compile(optimizer=keras.optimizers.Adam(LR), loss='mse')
model.summary()

# TRAINING
data_gen = generate_fake_videos()
model.fit(data_gen, steps_per_epoch=100, epochs=EPOCHS)

# PREDICTION
test_batch: np.ndarray = next(generate_fake_videos(1))
recon: np.ndarray = model.predict(test_batch)
error: np.ndarray = np.mean((recon - test_batch)**2, axis=(1,2,3,4))
print("Reconstruction error:", error)

# THRESHOLD
THR: float = 0.02
anomalous_flags = error > THR
print("Anomaly detected in sequence? ", anomalous_flags)

Key Notes (few sentences):

  • Core logic is in the hybrid ConvLSTM autoencoder + Transformer encoder layers for spatio-temporal representation.
  • Uses fake/random batches; replace generate_fake_videos() with UCSD or UCF dataset loader.
  • Huge compute; best run with GPU.
  • Hyperparameters like SEQ_LEN, head_size, ff_dim, LR, and THR should be tuned for your production setup.

Research reference: This approach follows similar architecture in video anomaly detection systems using ConvLSTM and Transformer attention (medium.com, arxiv.org, arxiv.org, researchgate.net)

  • Optional GAN discriminator for adversarial training.
